title: 2024 Knox Legal Studies Trial
notes: Question 3 appears ambiguous: A and C describe the same rebuttable presumption for a 14-year-old. The question section contains no shared stimuli or figures.

questions.stem:
Sophia is a New Zealand citizen who has served a 7-year jail sentence for aggravated assault.
Which post-sentencing consideration would most likely apply to Sophia?

options.C: Continued detention
options.D: Forfeiture of assets

questions.stem:
Frank has been arrested and detained by police.
To ensure any information provided by Frank during questioning is admissible in court, what must police do?

options.C: Caution Frank as to his rights
options.D: Keep written and audio copies of police interviews

questions.stem:
A 14 year old has been charged with armed robbery.
Which of the following is true?

options.B: This is a District Court matter.
options.C: A rebuttable presumption applies.
options.D: This is a Children’s Court matter.

questions.answerNote: Doli incapax (a rebuttable presumption) covers 10 to 13 only, so A and C are both false for a 14-year-old; Armed robbery (s 97, max 20 years) is not a serious children's indictable offence, so the Children's Court hears it. A/C are the equivalent distractors.

questions.stem: Human rights in Australia are best protected when they are

options.C: incorporated into domestic laws.
options.D: monitored by the United Nations.

questions.stem:
A victim impact statement is presented in court for a high-profile murder case. The judge fails to consider the statement before deciding upon the offender’s sentence.
What is this an example of?

options.C: The impact of the media
options.D: A miscarriage of justice

questions.answerNote: 'Fails to consider' suggests a procedural error (miscarriage of justice); A (judicial discretion) is plausible because the court may decide what weight a victim impact statement gets.

questions.stem: Which of the following rights is recognised by the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights (1976)?

options.B: The right to freedom of religion
options.C: The right to live free of torture and slavery
options.D: The right to participate in the election of government

questions.stem: Which of the following is a role of a Public Defender?

options.A: To provide general legal advice to the public
options.B: To prove a defendant’s innocence on the balance of probabilities
options.C: To prove a defendant’s innocence beyond reasonable doubt
options.D: To cross-examine the Prosecution’s witness

questions.stem:
Stanley, 15 years old, has been detained and is being questioned by police.
Which of the following is true regarding his interrogation?

options.A: A lawyer must be present at the interview.
options.B: One of Stanley’s parents must be present at the interview.
options.C: Stanley must agree to the support person present at the interview.
options.D: Stanley can refuse to have any support person present at the interview.

questions.stem: Continued detention best reflects which of the following purposes of punishment?

options.C: General deterrence
options.D: Retribution

questions.stem: Why may Legal Aid NOT be granted for a criminal case?

options.A: The Director of Public Prosecutions declines the accused’s request.
options.B: The police determine the offender doesn’t qualify for Legal Aid.
options.C: The accused does not meet the means test requirement.
options.D: The matter is a strictly indictable offence.

questions.stem: Albert, an Australian citizen, is arrested for international arms trafficking. His trial will fall under the jurisdiction of which of the following?

options.C: A United Nations ad hoc tribunal
options.D: The International Court of Justice

questions.stem:
Police charge a 16 year old with drink driving.
In which court will the matter be heard?

options.C: District
options.D: Local

questions.stem:
Person A provides stolen security access codes to a bank. Person B demands money from a teller while holding a gun. Person C keeps bank employees under control. Person D drives the getaway vehicle.
Who are the principal offenders in this scenario?

options.C: Persons A, B and C
options.D: Persons A and D

questions.stem: Who will determine whether illegally obtained evidence is admissible in the trial of a murder suspect?

options.C: A Supreme Court judge
options.D: A magistrate in a committal conference

questions.stem: Which is true of peace rights and environmental rights?

options.B: They are necessary for other human rights to be protected.
options.C: They were among the first human rights to be recognised.
options.D: They are protected under the United Nations Charter (1945).

questions.stem: Which of the following can be a crime against humanity?

options.C: Piracy
options.D: Money laundering

questions.answerNote: Rape is expressly listed as a crime against humanity (Rome Statute art 7); Genocide (B) is a separate core crime, though sometimes loosely treated as one.

questions.stem: Which best describes ‘recklessness’ under criminal law?

options.A: A partial defence; The accused fails to understand the seriousness of their actions
options.B: A partial defence; The accused is suffering from a mental illness when they act
options.C: A form of mens rea; The accused fails to foresee a risk which they should have foreseen
options.D: A form of mens rea; The accused foresees a risk, but does the action anyway

questions.stem: What is a subpoena?

options.A: An amount of money provided as a financial guarantee during bail
options.B: A legal document requiring a witness to give evidence in court or produce documents
options.C: A legal document permitting police to search a premises or intercept communications
options.D: A legal document stating when and where an accused person must appear to answer charges

questions.stem: Which of the following involves both a human rights and criminal law issue in Australia?

options.B: A child is forced to work in a factory
options.C: A temporary VISA holder commits an assault
options.D: A same-sex couple is denied the right to marry

questions.stem: The United Nations Human Rights Council is

options.C: an intergovernmental organisation
options.D: an independent statutory authority

questions.answerNote: The Human Rights Council is an intergovernmental body within the United Nations.
